reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays and adds isNonWorkingDay, and the two server handlers share a local applyWeekendHandling, but getNextDate and schedule-template each re-derive the skip-vs-move rule instead of using one definition.

duplication.why: The 'daily and skipWeekend' test is written four times (getNextDate, applyWeekendHandling, getUpcomingDates, schedule-template) and getNextDate re-implements the filter-then-move logic of applyWeekendHandling.

placement.why: applyWeekendHandling, the rule's fullest expression, sits privately in server/schedules/app.ts while the same rule is coded separately in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate, where this tree keeps schedule date rules.

scope.why: Edits are confined to schedule date logic, its parsing, type, handler and tests.

maintainability.why: Readable, but the rule lives in two layers with repeated frequency checks, noSkipWeekend is reused as a 'daily skip' switch by the template, and scan/padding sizes are ad-hoc constants.

bypasses_abstraction.where: budget/schedule-template.ts keeps its own skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend : date ternary and toggles getNextDate's noSkipWeekend by its own isDaily check; getNextDate does not use applyWeekendHandling.

disguised_duplication.where: getNextDate's find(!(skipsWeekendDays && isNonWorkingDay)) + movesWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend reshapes applyWeekendHandling's filter/map in server/schedules/app.ts.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; getNextDate gains the daily-skip/move special case; schedule-template.ts and getUpcomingDates' own daily take computation decide parts of the rule outside the shared function.
